companions.label: Birch
companions.readableText: Birch is the Betula genus, a lineage of trees associated with light, renewal and new beginnings. This companion is a genus study, not one individual tree.
companions.artworkCaption: Supplied Circle artwork · genus study, not documentary photography.

companions.label: The Great London Plane of Ely
companions.readableText: The Great London Plane of Ely is an individual Platanus × hispanica. Research alias: Bishop’s Plane, recorded by Paul Wood, entry 437. Ed confirmed the same-tree identity from the supplied research records. No permanent S33D Ancient Friend profile has been created.
companions.artworkCaption: Council illustration · its printed Ancient Friend heading does not establish a published Atlas profile. Research alias: Bishop’s Plane (Paul Wood).

companions.label: Rose
companions.readableText: Rose is the Rosa genus. This flower companion invites attention to beauty, relationship, pollen, shelter and hips.
details: Flower and pollination · spring to summer
companions.artworkCaption: Supplied Circle artwork · the plate’s nectar wording is awaiting correction; this text uses pollen.

companions.label: Tomato
companions.readableText: Tomato, Solanum lycopersicum, is a cultivated plant whose flowers and developing fruit invite attention to care, nourishment and seasonal change.
companions.artworkCaption: Supplied Circle artwork · plant study, not an identification guide.

companions.label: Bay Bolete
companions.readableText: Bay Bolete, Imleria badia, is a woodland fungus living in partnership with tree roots. This illustration is not an identification or foraging guide.
companions.artworkCaption: Supplied Circle artwork · the plate’s Edible label is awaiting correction and must not be used as eating advice.
companions.safety: Look closely, leave it growing. Never eat a wild mushroom on the strength of a picture.

companions.label: Toucan
companions.readableText: Toucan names the bird family Ramphastidae. The companion explores forest life, seed dispersal, movement and relationships with trees.
companions.artworkCaption: Supplied Circle artwork · family-level companion, not a verified species record.

companions.label: Winnie-the-Pooh
companions.readableText: Winnie-the-Pooh is the book by A. A. Milne, first published in 1926. It joins the Circle as a literary work, with themes of friendship, imagination, play and place.
companions.artworkCaption: Book companion · text-only presentation while replacement artwork is reviewed. No character image or quotation is shown.

welcome: Come as you are: listen, wander, meet a companion, or simply sit by the Fire. Nothing is asked of you.
